Signal Ledger

Lay out a bull and bear read as grouped rows, each naming the signal it rests on and its evidence, with observed rows kept apart from the author's judgment.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1Group header27 Section label (h3) left, row count right, one hairline under ittext-secondary, border
2RowA list item on one hairline; three columns from a 58rem container (chip, signal, evidence), two from 38rem (chip over signal, evidence), one belowborder
3Chip28 Chip naming the view (Bull, Bear, Rules, Call); never wraps, so the chip column is 10rem wide at three columnsplain, cyan, gold
4SignalMono, sentence case (caps on a long label fail the all-caps rule) label: what the view rests on, with its grade in brackets (leading, lagging, noisy)text-secondary, --ds-font-mono
5EvidenceBody text with the source linked inline; a dated figure where one existstext
6Judgment railA 2px gold rule down the left of a judgment group's rowsgold

Usage

Use it when

  • A view on a market or a decision is argued from both sides and each side should name the signal it rests on.
  • The author's own call must read as judgment, apart from what was observed.

Do not use it when

  • Do not colour a view green or red before it has settled: in ARCS green means proven and red means failed.
  • Do not use it for a plain fact table with no sides; that is a table.
  • Do not put a row in a judgment group without the word that marks it as yours (My read, My view).

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
groups[]{label, judgment?, rows[]}yeslabel is one or two words (Observed, My judgment, Reading errors); judgment: true draws the gold rail.
rows[]{chip, tone, signal, text}yestone is plain (unsettled view), cyan (a sourced, dated fact) or gold (judgment or a limit). Every observed row cites its source in text.

Access

  • Each group is a section labelled by its h3; rows are a ul, so a screen reader announces the count.
  • The grid uses minmax(0,1fr) and rem sizes, so the largest text size and roomy spacing wrap inside the row.
  • Colour is never the only signal: the chip names the view and the judgment group says My judgment in its label.
